author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: Techs Lift Stock Market, But Health Care Sector Stands OutTechs Lift Stock Market, But This Other Sector Stands Out | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The technology sector climbed Thursday, helping the Nasdaq composite lead stocks with a gain of nearly 0.7%. But the health care sector was even stronger.
X Meanwhile, Tesla ( TSLA ) shares plummeted nearly 10% after the regular session on reports that the SEC charged CEO Elon Musk with securities fraud .
Biotech, pharmaceutical and health provider stocks led the market. IBD's generic drugs industry group jumped 2%. The managed care and medical research equipment groups climbed at least 1%. The SPDR Health Care ETF ( XLV ) rose 0.5% to a new closing high.
Technology certainly had its share of leadership. Various software groups rose about 1% or more. Internet content added more than 1%. The Philadelphia semiconductor index, or the SOX, is trying to bounce after falling to the 200-day moving average. It rose 0.5% Thursday.
Major techs Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ) rose 1% to 2%. No doubt, their gains helped the Nasdaq outperform.
The S&P 500 climbed 0.3%, ending a four-day losing streak. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 0.2%, halting a mild three-day skid. The two indexes, however, faded in the final three hours of the session, and the S&P 500 closed near the day's lows.
Small caps lagged, with the Russell 2000 down a fraction after giving up gains. The index has been trending downward this month.
Volume fell from Wednesday's totals, based on preliminary trading data. Advancers led declines by 5-to-4 on the NYSE and were nearly even on the Nasdaq.
Dow component Nike ( NKE ) rose 1% and erased the entire loss from Wednesday, which followed the company's earnings report. Nike shares are in buy range from an 81.10 buy point and from a pullback to the 10-week moving average.
The IBD 50 was up 0.4% late Thursday. CyberArk ( CYBR ) was the best performing component, up more than 7% as the cybersecurity company rose from support at the 10-week moving average in big volume. The stock was added to IBD Leaderboard .
A few other medical-related IBD 50 stocks also did well. Health Insurance Innovations ( HIIQ ) and medical software firm Veeva Systems ( VEEV ) are near new highs. Biotech company Ligand Pharmaceuticals ( LGND ) hit a new high.
Also in the IBD 50 , Planet Fitness ( PLNT ) had a second straight lackluster day, closing near session lows after surrendering gains. Still, the fitness center chain held barely above the 53.51 buy point of a breakout on Tuesday.
Despite the market's strength, there were no breakouts among high-rated stocks Thursday. A few peeked above buy points, but their price and volume action was lackluster.
